1.text:
s = 40 + 2t

The equation gives the speed s, in miles per hour, of a certain car t seconds after it began to accelerate. What is the speed, in miles per hour, of the car 3 seconds after it began to accelerate?

2.text: Which of the following equations best represents the line of best fit shown?
2._note: Question badge is scrolled off the top of page 56; number inferred from the 1 → 3 sequence.
2.showWork: The line rises from left to right, so the slope is positive: +1.7, which rules out B and D. It crosses the y-axis above the origin (near y = 0.8), so the y-intercept is positive, which rules out C. Only y = 0.8 + 1.7x has both a positive intercept and a positive slope.

3.text: The width of a rectangle is 5 centimeters. The length of the rectangle is 30 centimeters longer than the width. What is the area, in square centimeters, of this rectangle?
3.showWork: Length = 5 + 30 = 35 cm. Area = length × width = 35(5) = 175 square centimeters.

4.text: If 7 + x = 3, what is the value of 56 + 8x?

5.text: In one week in 2017, a technician earned a total of $1,055 by working at her regular job and at a second job doing part-time work. The equation 20h + 17c = 1,055 represents this situation, where h is the number of hours worked at her regular job and c is the number of hours worked at her second job. Which of the following is the best interpretation of 20 in this context?

choices.A: The amount, in dollars, the technician earned for each hour she worked at her regular job
choices.B: The amount, in dollars, the technician earned for each hour she worked at her second job
choices.C: The number of hours the technician worked in one week at her regular job
choices.D: The number of hours the technician worked in one week at her second job

5.showWork: In 20h + 17c = 1,055 the variable h counts hours at the regular job, so 20 multiplies those hours to give dollars. Its units are dollars per hour at the regular job.

6.text:
The table shows the frequency of values in a data set.

What is the minimum value of the data set?
6.showWork: The data values are 20, 26, 32, and 38 (the second column gives how many times each occurs, not data values). The smallest value listed is 20.

y = 5x^2 + 5

9.text: The expression 19x^5 + 20x^5 − 10x^5 is equivalent to bx^5, where b is a constant. What is the value of b?
9.showWork: All three terms are like terms: 19 + 20 − 10 = 29, so the expression equals 29x^5 and b = 29.

10.text: The point (v, −5) lies on the line shown. What is the value of v?
10._note: Question badge is scrolled off the top of page 64; number inferred from the 9 → 11 sequence.
10.showWork: The line passes through (−12, 0) and (0, −11), so its slope is (−11 − 0)/(0 − (−12)) = −11/12 and its equation is y = −(11/12)x − 11. Setting y = −5: −5 = −(11/12)v − 11, so (11/12)v = −6 and v = −72/11.

11.text:
f(x) = 22

For the given linear function f, which table gives three values of x and their corresponding values of f(x)?
11._note: Stem plus choices A–B are on page 66; page 65 is the scrolled view showing A–C. Choice D is cut off on both captures and was reconstructed from the identical item on the parallel form 2025 March Int-A (f(x) = 29, choice D = 29 / 0 / −29), where D is fully visible. The key is unaffected: B is the only constant table.
11.showWork: f is the constant function 22, so f(x) = 22 for every x, including x = 0, 1, and 2.

12.text: In the figure shown, line k intersects lines r and s. If w = 146, which additional piece of information is sufficient to prove that lines r and s are parallel?
12._note: Stem and figure from page 68 (top view); page 67 is the scrolled view showing all four choices.
12.showWork: w° and x° are a linear pair, so x = 34 no matter what — A is always true and proves nothing; the same is true of y + z = 180 in D. C would force y = 34, which makes the lines not parallel. w° and y° are corresponding angles, so r ∥ s exactly when y = w = 146.

13.text: Which expression is equivalent to (133y)^(1/2), where y > 1?
13.showWork: A rational exponent of 1/2 is a square root of the whole base: (133y)^(1/2) = √(133y).

f(x) = −26(2)^(x/6)

Which table gives four values of x and their corresponding values of f(x) for the given exponential function?
14._note: Stem from page 70 (choice D clipped); page 71 is the scrolled view with all four choice tables.

15.text: The measure of angle B is 3π/4 radians. What is the value of sin(B)?
15.showWork: 3π/4 radians is 135°, a second-quadrant angle with reference angle 45°. Sine is positive in the second quadrant, so sin(3π/4) = sin(45°) = √2/2.

16.text: A school is ordering tablet computers for its students. The tablets cost $164 each, and 6% tax is added to the total cost of the order. If the school can spend no more than 44,800 dollars on the tablets, including tax, what is the maximum number of tablets that the school can order?
16.showWork: With tax each tablet costs 164(1.06) = $173.84. Solving 173.84n ≤ 44,800 gives n ≤ 257.7, so at most 257 tablets (257 cost $44,676.88; 258 would cost $44,850.72).

17.text: A triangular prism has a height of 3 centimeters (cm) and a volume of 60 cm^3. What is the area, in cm^2, of the base of the prism? (The volume of a triangular prism is equal to Bh, where B is the area of the base and h is the height of the prism.)
17.showWork: V = Bh gives 60 = B(3), so B = 60/3 = 20 square centimeters.

18.text: The graph of y = f(x) is shown, where f(x) = ab^x + c, and a, b, and c are constants. For how many values of x does f(x) = 0?
18._note: Stem and figure from page 75 (choices C–D clipped); page 76 is the scrolled view with all four choices.
18.showWork: The graph never touches the x-axis: it approaches the horizontal asymptote y = −5 on the left and falls without bound on the right, staying below the x-axis everywhere. Since ab^x is always negative here and c = −5, f(x) < −5 < 0 for every x, so f(x) = 0 has zero solutions.

19.text:
x(x + 4) − 140 = 3x(x − 10)

What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
19.showWork: Expand: x^2 + 4x − 140 = 3x^2 − 30x, so 0 = 2x^2 − 34x + 140, i.e. x^2 − 17x + 70 = 0. The sum of the solutions is 17 (the roots are 7 and 10).

20.text:
−3x^2 − 7x + 1 = 0

What is the greatest solution to the given equation?
20.showWork: Multiply by −1: 3x^2 + 7x − 1 = 0. The quadratic formula gives x = (−7 ± √(49 + 12))/6 = −7/6 ± √61/6. The greater root uses the plus sign: −7/6 + √61/6.

21.text: In triangle ABC, BC = 36√3. What is the value of cos A?
21._note: Grid-in: .5 and 0.5 are mathematically equivalent forms of this answer.
21.showWork: Angle B is right and angle C = 30°, so angle A = 180 − 90 − 30 = 60°. cos A = cos 60° = 1/2. The side length 36√3 is not needed.

22.text: The positive number a is 2,047% of the sum of the positive numbers b and c, and b is 89% of c. What percent of b is a?
